summary: Highest per-capita incident load in the country: 72 recorded anti-LGBTQ incidents in 2025 in a state of ~1.4m. Counterweight: in July 2026 a county court found an attacker violated the NH Civil Rights Act after striking a trans gas-station employee, using his pronoun refusal as bias evidence, with bodycam showing officers correcting his pronoun use — institutions working. Slightly below the national score 0.36.

sources.summary: GLAAD ALERT Desk release (January 2025): 1,042 anti-LGBTQ incidents tracked in 2025 across 47 states and the District of Columbia — 128 vandalism, 76 violent assaults, 22 mass-violence threats, 15 arson attempts; 51% of incidents targeted transgender and gender-nonconforming people, up 10% on 2024. Per-state tallies give this state 72 recorded incidents — second-highest national total from a population of ~1.4m, i.e. the highest per-capita load.

NHPR/Concord Monitor (July 2026): the Merrimack County Superior Court found a man who physically and verbally assaulted a transgender woman at her workplace in May 2024 violated the New Hampshire Civil Rights Act — ordering three years' no contact (350 ft from her, her home and workplace) and a $5,000 fine, alongside a separate guilty plea to second-degree assault with a suspended sentence; the Attorney General's office treated his refusal to use her pronouns, captured on bodycam during questioning, as evidence of bias motive.

tangentialFactors: Anti-trans campaigners took legal action against a small school district over a trans athlete — local climate pressure rather than a statewide rule, but part of the same visibility conflict.
